A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MiniLongBench research work. All 19 pages, including Appendices A–H, are readable, and text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables and results.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, timing measurements, rank correlations and ablations in Sections 2–5, with additional model results and analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including detailed model scores, sensitivity analyses and repeated timing measurements in the appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same embedding/PCA preprocessing, logistic-regression representation learning and K-means selection. The predictive evaluation procedure in Section 4.2 and direct evaluation in Appendix G are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LongBench coverage and 237-sample MiniLongBench: six task categories and 21 tasks covering English, Chinese and code. Table 1 and Appendix A are unchanged.

E2.justification: The random-sampling comparisons and OpenAIEmbedding, Longformer and BERT alternatives retain the same participants. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 20 construction models, remaining-model validation, compression settings, task metrics and evaluation procedures. The model assignments in Appendix B and direct-evaluation protocol in Appendix G are identical.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains all analyses of dimension, PCA, encoder choice, compression ratio, bias and construction-model selection/count. The representation and ranking visualizations in Appendices E–F are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same sampling and repetition counts, including 10,000 subset draws, five repeats per construction-model count and 100 timing repeats in Appendix H. The statistical-significance statement in Section 5 is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including Figure 1's timings, Figure 5's overall Spearman correlation of 0.97, Table 2 and Appendix Tables 4–8. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the threshold-search reasoning and the task definition in Appendix A are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: a compact benchmark evaluated across over 60 LLMs, costing 4.5% of the original evaluation with approximately 0.97 rank correlation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of redundancy, representation learning and ranking discrepancies are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning performance-record acquisition costs, imperfect agreement with LongBench and weaker summarization/synthetic-task performance.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, model lists and Appendix H's hardware, storage and timing details are identical. The code/data/tutorial link also remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The citations, reference list and related-work discussion in Appendix D are unchanged, including the positioning relative to earlier benchmark-compression research.

P1.justification: v2 marks Liang Lin as corresponding author and adds the corresponding-author footnote. The arXiv version/date text is updated; the scientific prose and section/appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is slightly smaller, the first-page text reflows around the new footnote, and printed page numbers are removed throughout. Rendered pages 2–19 otherwise match exactly; no table or figure content changes.

improvement.justification: v2 adds administrative clarity through the corresponding-author note and makes minor layout adjustments. Removing printed page numbers slightly reduces navigation cues, but the scientific argument, evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain identical, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
